name: Toyota Customer Loyalty Models
listdetail: The Toyota Customer Loyalty Models predict the probability of a customer returning for a service or purchase of a new vehicle. This is relevant for all customers who currently own or have owned a Toyota in the past.
detail: The Toyota Customer Loyalty Models predict the probability of a customer returning for a service or purchase of a new vehicle. This is relevant for all customers who currently own or have owned a Toyota in the past. Customers who repair or buy parts from a Toyota Dealer have a higher likelihood of buying another Toyota or Lexus vehicle. There are currently four models available for this feature. Model 1: Toyota Return to Service Visit Model (Binary) This is a binary classifier that predicts if a customer will return to an authorized service center for service. Model 2: Toyota Return to Service Revenue Model (5 Class Multi-class) This is a multi-class classifier that predicts the spending potential of a customer after the customer is predicted to return for a service. This generates the probabilities for 5 different classes and based on the highest probability the customer is predicted for the given class. Model 3: Toyota Return to Purchase Visit Model (Binary) This is a binary classifier that predicts the probability of a customer returning to purchase a new vehicle. Model 4: Toyota Return to Purchase Revenue Model (6 Class Multi-class) This is a multi-class classifier that predicts the spending potential of a customer after the customer is predicted to return for a purchase of a new vehicle. This generates the probabilities for 6 different classes. A final spending value is predicted after complex data processing considering probabilities for all classes and their average purchase value. Some of the most important data sources for building these models are Customer Demographics Data, Toyota Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data.

name: Toyota In-Market Models
listdetail: The Toyota In-Market Models predict how likely a customer is to purchase a Toyota vehicle by a specific series or segment type within the next 12 months.
detail:
The Toyota In-Market Models predict how likely a customer is to purchase a Toyota vehicle by a specific series or segment type within the next 12 months. This applies to current Toyota owners and those who previously owned a Toyota in the last 15 years, but no longer own one today. These models help Marketing teams plan and execute in-market campaigns to existing customers and their lookalikes. It also helps optimize media-spend by enabling targeted marketing.

For customers predicted to be in-market, each model will return the probability that the customer will purchase a particular series or vehicle segment. Using this probability, we can determine how strong a customer''s in-market signal is. Depending on the business use case, the customer''s signal strength enables strategies that target only the most in-market customers.

All the models consist of Machine Learning (ML) data based on patterns & trends. Some of the most significant data sources for building these models are Customer Demographics Data, Toyota Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, Vehicle Configuration Data, and New Car Sales VIN Based Actuals Data.

detail:

Segmentation models consider multiple attributes based on customer purchase and service history with Toyota. Each customer is assigned to exactly one segment and sub-segment. Each segment of customers is homogeneous within and heterogeneous between other segments. When a customer is in the "Own" stage of the Shop-Buy-Own process, they would have higher-dimensional data available, which could be segmented in various ways. Understanding our customers better will enable us to improve our processes and spend according to their needs. This model contains both Toyota and Lexus data.

The Lexus Customer Loyalty Models predict the probability of a customer returning for a service or purchase of a new Lexus vehicle. This is relevant for all customers who currently own or have owned a Lexus in the past. Customers who repair or buy parts from a Lexus Dealer have a higher likelihood of buying another Lexus vehicle.

In this feature, there are two different stages: Owner Segmentation and Predictive Modeling.

Owner Segmentation: Lexus owners are segmented based on their current relationship and recent activities with Lexus Dealerships.

Predictive Modeling: Predicts the likelihood that a Lexus customer will return for purchase or service, as well as future growth potential at a customer level. \n\nSome of the most important data sources for building this model are Customer Demographics Data, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, and Customer Call Center.

detail:
With the Customer Descriptive Score Model, we can gain a comprehensive view of customer profile data regarding ownership, service, and engagement, which is essential for all aspects of customer interaction with the Toyota and Lexus brands.

This model is based on a customer's transactional behavior, which is broken down into the following scores.

Customer Ownership Score: A score indicating a customer's association with Toyota ownership. The calculation is based on factors such as historical ownerships, purchases, memberships, and associations.

Service RFM Score: This is a score reflecting the customer's historical interactions with service repair. It is calculated based on various factors such as Recency, Frequency, and Monetary aspects of the service visits.

Engagement Score: A score based on the customer's activity and usage of our products and services.

Survey Score: This score reflects a customer's level of satisfaction with a product, service, or support interaction based on survey responses.

Some of the major sources for this data model are Customer Demographics Data, Toyota Service History USA, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, and Customer Call Center.

name: Customer Survey - Sentiment and Emotion Detection Model
listdetail: The Sentiment Analysis and Emotion Detection Model provides insight into a customer's experience with a product or interaction with a company representative and identifies weak links that cause negative reactions.
detail:
The Sentiment Analysis and Emotion Detection Model provides insight into a customer's experience with a product or interaction with a company representative and identifies weak links that cause negative reactions. With its Voice of the Customer (VOC) text analytics and natural language processing (NLP) capabilities, this model significantly reduces the time and effort required to gain insights into unstructured text-based data.

Sentiment Analysis scores each verbatim on the strength of positive or negative sentiment, enabling us to classify the texts as “Positive”, “Negative”, or “Neutral”.  
This type of feedback helps us create a positive customer experience in the future and drive continuous improvement.

Emotion Detection identifies five emotions based on the words used verbatim: “Happy”, “Sad”, “Fear”, “Anger”, and “Surprise”. This enables you to prioritize feature categories based on the strength-of-feeling in addition to category prevalence across the customer base.

Some of the most important data sources for building this model are US Toyota Survey Data, US Lexus Survey Data, Vehicle Configuration Data, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, Customer Call Center, and Quality Campaigns.

name: Customer Survey - Topic Model
listdetail: This Customer Survey Topic Model can provide you with insights into trending topics and sub-topics that help deliver exactly what your customers need and increase positive business results.
detail:
This Customer Survey Topic Model can provide you with insights into trending topics and sub-topics that help deliver exactly what your customers need and increase positive business results. Utilizing Voice of the Customer (VOC) text analytics and natural language processing (NLP) capabilities, this model significantly reduces the time and effort required to gain an understanding of unstructured text-based data.

Below are some high-level features of the model:

The Unsupervised Topic modeling feature provides insight into the topics that are trending in a set of verbatims. Sub-topics enable you to dig deeper into each of those topics. This solution is purely data-driven – it analyzes the data itself without relying on any external information or domain knowledge. 

The Semi-Supervised Topic modeling feature enables you to guide the analysis of your data to capture certain expected topics. By doing so, it provides the benefits of supervised learning without requiring expensive and time-consuming data labeling. Semi-Supervised modeling corresponds to the historical Product Quality Survey (PQS) categories and subcategories, which facilitates analysis of the Feature Comments data based on these categories. The subtopics bring out themes within the topics themselves and provide insight into any verbatims that do not neatly fit into existing categories.

Some of the most important data sources for building this model are US Toyota Survey Data, US Lexus Survey Data, Vehicle Configuration Data, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, Customer Call Center, and Quality Campaigns.

name: Smart Window ETA Model
listdetail: The Smart Window ETA model predicts when a vehicle will be delivered to the dealer at various stages of its lifecycle, starting with dealer assignment and continuing until it is delivered to the dealer. By using a predictive ETA, we can reduce wasted overhead and transportation delays, as well as make informed decisions concerning inventory planning.
detail:
The Smart Window ETA model predicts when a vehicle will be delivered to the dealer at various stages of its lifecycle, starting with dealer assignment and continuing until it is delivered to the dealer. By using a predictive ETA, we can reduce wasted overhead and transportation delays, as well as make informed decisions concerning inventory planning.

The delivery window is updated at major manufacturing and transportation events to provide an accurate estimated delivery window at dealerships from the time of dealer assignment through the manufacturing process and transportation journey. 

This algorithm is based on Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (UETA) data using events from the most recent 90 days for hundreds of vehicles. Only valid VINs were analyzed during data processing (i.e. those with a valid delivery code). Traded vehicles are taken into account only once they have been delivered for the first time. Any VINs with a "hold" have been filtered out.
 
A tree-based modeling approach has been used to predict time-to-delivery from events received for each VIN. The clusters of points obtained at different leaf nodes of the CART decision tree were explored during this process. Using a typical tree-based model, the prediction outcome is an aggregated value of observations at the leaf node. However, our analysis showed that observations at the leaf nodes are not necessarily homogeneous and follow a gamma distribution. By aggregating all of those values, hidden trends in those distributions would be masked.
Therefore, we regressed the "time-to-delivery" against deciles of distributions. At leaf node, minimum window refers to absolute minimum value, and maximum window refers to x-intersection of decile regression line at one.

The model predicts each VIN's every event (limited to only post-FQA events in phase 1), where a window is provided. It is most likely that vehicles will be delivered between the Start Date and the End Date of windows.

detail:
This dashboard provides an array of in-depth Toyota Motor Manufacturing, Indiana, Inc. (TMMI) West Paint reports containing information on equipment and operations essential for cost efficiency, process planning, increasing safety and productivity, improving on-time delivery, and analyzing trends. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM01 Cost Analysis by Equipment: The following report provides an overview of the costs associated with equipment. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM02 Detail Cost Analysis by Equipment Report: This report breaks down the previous list into a more detailed description of what we spent on certain equipment assets. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM03 Faults 10 to 19 Minutes Line Report: This report provides a list of all Faults that occur between 10 - 19 minutes. If a Fault lasts longer than 19 minutes, it becomes a larger issue causing extended downtime and should be escalated to a priority for repairs. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM04 Process Report: This report shows a breakdown of all the processes at the facility, along with the associated Equipment Stops and Line Stops. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM05 Major Breakdown Faults Report: This report lists the major breakdowns (anything over 19 minutes), the Build Date Start, the Line Stop, the Equipment Stop, and the Fault description. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM06 West Paint Equipment Summary Report: This report provides the number of Faults, Line Stops, and Equipment Stops across all equipment on-site. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM07 Repetitive Faults Report: This report is meant to capture repetitive equipment Faults so that we can track and resolve repair issues.

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM08 Summary Floor Conveyor Report: This report contains a list of floor conveyor groups and the total amount of equipment Faults and Line Stops. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM09 Totals of All Equipment Detail Report Production: This report breaks down all equipment into major areas with the total number of Faults, Stop times, and an explanation of each Fault during production hours. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM10 Totals of All Equipment Details Report: This report breaks down all equipment into major areas with the total number of Faults, Stop times, and an explanation of each Fault that occurred throughout the entire work day. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM11 Totals of All Non-Equipment Details Report: Similar to the previous report but lists Non-Equipment downtime with the total number of Faults, Stop times, and an explanation of each Fault that occurred outside of active production. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM12 Totals Floor Conveyor Detail Report: This report contains a list of floor conveyors, along with the total amount of equipment Faults and Line Stops. 

TMMI Paint INT1 EOM13 Totals Robot Detail Report: It contains information about the robots on the floor, as well as Faults, Stop times, and Work Order descriptions.

name: Body Weld Inspection Model
listdetail: The Body Weld Inspection Model is designed to assess the quality of spot welding between the car's body and the rocker panel.
detail:
The Body Weld Inspection Model is designed to assess the quality of spot welding between the car's body and the rocker panel. Through the use of image processing, this model is able to identify weld quality easier and in less time with less manual intervention. As a result of using the data provided, the quality of the vehicles or units being produced will be improved and scrap will be reduced. Utilizing this information can also improve the maintenance requirements on the robots used to do the welds by identifying if the maintenance is being performed on a timely basis.

This model will determine the threshold value for dividing No Good Welds from Good Welds and show better bifurcation (ratio) between the two groups. These values are obtained using logistic regression. To detect the centroid of a weld in an image, Yolov4 Object (how it works - series of division techniques) is used and then an average 1D value is calculated around the centroid. For each individual pixel, the 1D value represents the temperature difference between frames. By comparing the average 1D value of the specified frame to the threshold value, the weld quality can be predicted.

Thermal Wave Imaging photos are used as input to the model from Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky (TMMK). The spot weld is captured with a thermal imaging camera for one, two, or three seconds. DCB files are used to store these frames (images). Weld quality is determined by further processing of the DCB files into NumPy files.

Using the Toyota Digital Manufacturing platform, the model output is displayed via Poke Yoke with the latest 4 Weld status.

detail: This API service is used by applications to convert the category of a vehicle in inventory to a Demo category (“L”). Demo vehicles are part of a dealer’s inventory, but they are labeled as Demo to allow the dealer to submit warranty claims for that VIN. For warranty eligibility, vehicles must be sold to a customer before they receive a Date of First Use, but Demo vehicles get a DOFU before they are sold. Dealers use Demo cars for test drives or special sales events, but ultimately sell them as new via the Retail Delivery Report (RDR) process just like any other new vehicle. As part of the Demo processing provided by this API, the odometer reading is provided by the dealer when the vehicle is converted to Demo.

name: Retention Parts Propensity Models
listdetail: Retention Parts Propensity Models are used to predict how likely it is that a customer will visit a Toyota or Lexus dealership for specific parts within the next month.
detail:
Retention Parts Propensity Models are available for batteries, brakes, wipers, tires, and oil. Through these models, it is possible to anticipate which vehicles might need a specific part and to communicate with the customer in a timely manner. This helps optimize marketing, improve customer experience for Parts and Service marketing campaigns, and retain customer loyalty. Email campaigns support email marketing efforts for these parts-related campaigns by predicting which customers are most likely to purchase the respective key retention part. Digital campaigns support Digital marketing efforts for parts-related campaigns which are conducted on various Toyota websites or social media platforms. All the key parts of Propensity Models are utilized by media agencies to derive strategies around audiences generated by these models.
 
The Retention Parts Propensity Models are relevant to all customers who have owned or previously owned a Toyota or Lexus. These models predict a likely outcome at the customer level and can be used for a wide variety of business operations. From millions of existing Toyota customers, these models identify only those who are most likely to require retention parts.
 
Data collected from a broad range of sources is used in all of the models to study patterns and trends. Some of the most important data sources for building these models are Toyota Service History USA, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, Vehicle Configuration Data, Direct Parts Specifications and Tracking . Datasets like these are crucial to building hundreds of features for training models. For more details, please contact the Customer Data Science (CUDS) team.
 
These Propensity Models predict how likely it is that a customer will visit a Toyota dealership for these specific retention parts within the next month. Each propensity score is calculated at VIN level and a customer can likely have different scores for each VIN owned. A binary prediction value of 1 means that the VIN/Customer is predicted to purchase the specific retention part within a month, while a binary prediction value of 0 means that the VIN/Customer is not likely to purchase the particular part.

name: Mileage Estimator
listdetail: Based on historical trends and service history data, this model estimates mileage for each Toyota VIN at the end of the current month as well as the following six months.
detail: The Mileage Estimator model estimates miles for each VIN at the end of the current month and the end of the following month. It can also forecast the mileage of each VIN for the next six months. This model allows Parts and Services marketing campaigns to target customers based on their mileages. It can also be used for understanding the average VIN miles at the Regional or National level for each Series Type. Additionally, it assists with In-Market Campaigns by identifying the age of the VIN. Data collected from a broad range of sources is used in all of the models to study patterns and trends. Some of the most important data sources for building these models are Toyota Service History USA, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, and Vehicle Configuration Data. Based on historical trends, it takes into account specific Series, Model Year, and time-since-first-use combinations, as well as industry averages, standard grids, and miles driven since recent service visits by VIN. Subcomponents of this feature are comprised of Standard Vehicle Miles Grids that have been combined in various ways. Before returning a final estimate at the VIN level, the Mileage Estimator model often refers to these standard grids and industry averages. With this feature, you can perform advanced backfilling and exponential smoothing, making it extremely reliable. The feature is currently available for all Toyota VINs (including Scions) with a Date Of First Use within the last 15 years. Lexus VINs are not included. Presently, this feature covers approximately 30 million VINs. Standard Vehicle Miles Grid 1 - This grid is built at Make, Series, Model Year, Months Since DOFU, Percentiles (0-100), and studies the last 15 years of service history. This grid has a miles smoothing mechanism across months-since-DOFU and percentiles. Standard Vehicle Miles Grid 2 - This grid is built at Make, Series, Months Since DOFU, Percentiles (0-100) combination, and studies the last 15+ years of service history. This grid does back-filling of miles at different percentiles and months since DOFU. Once the backfilling is complete, a miles smoothing mechanism is applied across months-since-DOFU and percentiles. Additionally, the grid forecasts the future for the next six months.
